final.why: Unchanged: with a €200,000 cash budget and 3.5-8% in taxes and fees added on top of the price depending on the country, a €185,000 cap keeps the total purchase inside budget everywhere.
Unchanged: the plan asks for a small flat with one or two bedrooms, so studios and larger family homes are left out.

The only change this round: v2 found 70 matches, just over the 60 ceiling, so the after-costs return floor rises slightly from 6.0% to 6.2%; this trims the weakest tail while keeping both cities, since fairly-priced Bari flats net in the low 6s and Lodz's best reach about 7%.

Unchanged: the near-miss list confirms it is doing its job by blocking the €5,000-17,000 Bari listings with impossible 19-123% 'yields' that are almost certainly wrecks - exactly the big-repairs homes the buyer wants flagged.
Unchanged: an agency needs an active local rental market to find long-term tenants quickly, and all six matching zones have between 26 and 486 rental listings.
Unchanged guard: only countries where house prices rose at least about 3% last year are allowed, and all three candidates pass (Portugal 17.8%, Poland 5.9%, Italy 5.2%).
Unchanged: the search stays inside the three chosen cities, all within three hours' flight of Amsterdam and open to a Dutch buyer without any permit.
